prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is a general, enabling method: ligand design made arylamine formation routine across pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and materials. It has more than twenty-five years of independent confirmation and a well-established mechanism (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination). The attribution is as clean as this list offers: Buchwald and Hartwig independently produced the general ligand-controlled systems. It also has real cross-committee support. Four members ranked it in their top four and two put it first, which is a different kind of support from the narrower enthusiasms behind some other candidates. This is not an area of my own research. I therefore weigh it on breadth of use, mechanistic evidence and the quality of the structural and mechanistic characterisation of the catalytic intermediates, and on all three it holds up.
statement.case_against: The 2010 prize already honoured Pd cross-coupling, so a second prize in the family can look like repetition and the committee should be able to state clearly why C-N bond formation is a distinct advance. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work and Migita's precedent are not captured by a two-name citation, and the choice to exclude them must be defensible. The newer, faster-moving candidates (degraders, condensates) may represent bigger conceptual shifts, and awarding another mature synthetic method delays them. I do not think those arguments outweigh maturity and clarity, but they are the strongest reservation.

responses.point: Somfai ranks B057 first as a general method with visible use in process chemistry and total synthesis, and acknowledges that Kosugi and Migita deserve mention but would still go with a two-person prize.
responses.response: I agree with the two-person configuration and with the view that the evidence for generality is in the literature rather than in a single paper. I would go further than Somfai on one point. Kosugi's tin-amide coupling established the basic reactivity but was limited by toxic reagents and narrow scope, so the general catalytic method that everybody uses came later with Buchwald's and Hartwig's ligand systems. The citation wording should say general and catalytic, so that precedent is acknowledged without a third name. I am less convinced by Somfai's alternatives, photoredox and C-H functionalisation, whose credit is more diffuse and whose practical reach is still narrower.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks the PROTAC and molecular-glue field first as a new pharmacological principle, while placing B057 fourth and flagging possible overlap with the 2010 palladium prize.
responses.response: The overlap concern is fair and I take it seriously, but I think it is answerable: the 2010 citation was for C-C bond formation, and C-N coupling needed a separate set of mechanistic and ligand solutions. I accept that degraders are a genuinely new principle. My reservation is that the committee has not yet separated the chemistry from the drug-development momentum: there is no approved PROTAC, and the credit splits into two strands (PROTAC concept versus cereblon glue mechanism) with at least six strong names. A prize that must leave out Sakamoto, Handa or Ito is harder to defend than one for B057.

responses.point: Chabes places B068 first, crediting Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and argues that degraders turn protein removal into a designable chemical event with a clear mechanism.
responses.response: I do not dispute the novelty. My question is about structural evidence: for molecular glues, the cereblon mechanism rests on crystal structures of ternary complexes that came after the drugs were in use, and for PROTACs the ternary-complex structures are still a minority of cases. I would want the committee to confirm that the mechanistic story is as established as the clinical one before treating B068 as mature. I also note that Chabes's own top three includes Shokat's covalent KRAS work, with a cleaner single-laureate attribution that may be a better candidate than the degrader configuration.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, ranks condensates first and B057 second, and notes that B057 is fully mature and unambiguous in impact but follows the 2010 prize. He ranks halide perovskites fourth and flags that stability and lead toxicity make recognition possibly premature.
responses.response: We agree that B057 is mature, and I take his ranking of it second as support for it being the point where the committee can meet. On perovskites I share his maturity worry and, as a materials chemist, I would add that the structural chemistry of the phases (phase stability, ionic motion, defects) is still being worked out, which is why I keep B024 only as an alternative. I would ask for more evidence for condensates: the in vitro phase behaviour is clear, but the question of which condensates have a functional role in cells is still open, and that matters for a chemistry citation.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will see C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Whether the omission of Kosugi and Migita can be defended in the citation.
Whether degraders or condensates will turn out to be mature enough by the final ballot to displace B057 as the broadest-support option.
I have not been able to compare fields I know less well, such as computational chemistry and chemical biology, against B057 beyond what my colleagues have written.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B057 or the alternatives; my only connections are to electron crystallography and porous materials, which are not part of this configuration, and Stockholm University colleagueship with the Secretary, which is not a recusal issue.
